advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In test_a_redacting_mapping_stays_redacting, assert child is not caller_env and child["SYSTEMROOT"] == r"C:\Windows"
evidence: diff: `assert isinstance(child, SubprocessEnv)` / `assert "s3cret" not in repr(child)` / `assert "SYSTEMROOT" not in caller_env`
An identity return (`return env`) passes all three: the caller_env is a SubprocessEnv, its repr is redacted (tests/_subprocess_env.py:19-20), and it has no SYSTEMROOT
The diff adds no `child["SYSTEMROOT"] == ...` or `child is not caller_env` assertion to this test
advisory.finding: test_a_redacting_mapping_stays_redacting never checks that SYSTEMROOT was added to the returned child. If _child_env skipped the copy and returned the caller's SubprocessEnv unchanged, all three assertions would still pass, so the test cannot fail on the regression it is meant to catch.
scenarios: A refactor of the copy branch in _child_env (tests/_nested_pytest.py:56-57) drops the SYSTEMROOT insertion for dict subclasses; this test stays green
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert child is not caller_env` and `assert child["SYSTEMROOT"] == r"C:\Windows"` (also optionally `assert child["TOKEN"] == "s3cret"`).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the self-referential Windows expectation with an explicit literal such as {"PATH": "test-path", "SYSTEMROOT": os.environ["SYSTEMROOT"]}
advisory.finding: On Windows, test_the_call_contract_reaches_subprocess_run builds its expected env by calling _child_env(caller_env), the function under test. The test's only Windows-specific check, the env assertion, can therefore never disagree with the implementation.
scenarios: A _child_env bug on Windows (for example, forwarding extra ambient keys) produces the same wrong value on both sides of the assertion
advisory.suggested_fix: `assert captured["env"] == {"PATH": "test-path", "SYSTEMROOT": os.environ["SYSTEMROOT"]}` on nt, and assert `caller_env == {"PATH": "test-path"}` to confirm the caller's mapping was not mutated.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In test_a_redacting_mapping_stays_redacting, assert child["SYSTEMROOT"] == r"C:\Windows" and child is not caller_env
evidence: tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py:160-162: assert isinstance(child, SubprocessEnv) / assert "s3cret" not in repr(child) / assert "SYSTEMROOT" not in caller_env

Named violating input: SubprocessEnv({"PATH": "p", "TOKEN": "s3cret"}) with os_name="nt". An implementation that returns `env` for SubprocessEnv inputs passes all three assertions: it is a SubprocessEnv, its repr is redacted (tests/_subprocess_env.py:20), and the caller's object has no SYSTEMROOT.
The dict-only test at line 132 checks the added key, but only for a plain dict. It does not exercise the `type(env)(env)` branch for the SubprocessEnv subclass.
advisory.finding: test_a_redacting_mapping_stays_redacting never checks that the returned child contains SYSTEMROOT, or that it is a separate object from the caller's. It stays green if `_child_env` returns a SubprocessEnv unchanged on Windows. That is the exact case the fix targets: a minimal redacting env reaching a Windows child without SYSTEMROOT.
scenarios: A refactor special-cases SubprocessEnv to avoid copying and drops the SYSTEMROOT addition, so Windows children started with minimal_env-style or redacted envs die again with WinError 10106 while this unit test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert child is not caller_env` and `assert child["SYSTEMROOT"] == r"C:\Windows"` (and optionally `assert child["TOKEN"] == "s3cret"`) to test_a_redacting_mapping_stays_redacting.
